title: 10-Year Financial Forensics: FY2016–FY2025 & Capital Allocation

epigraph.quote: A decade of cash flow statements never lies: it tells you whether acquisitions compounded owner earnings or merely rented larger revenue.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: A ten-year historical review (FY2016–FY2025) highlights the core trade-offs of ABM's acquisition model [1, 24, 40]. Over this decade, revenue rose 70% from $5,144.7 million in FY2016 to $8,745.9 million in FY2025 [40]. This trajectory delivered a ~6.1% compound annual growth rate [40]. In contrast, GAAP net income and free cash flow followed a far more volatile path [24, 27]. Integration costs, pandemic disruptions in FY2020, and ELEVATE ERP investments weighed on cash conversion [24, 26, 27]. Higher interest expenses further dampened bottom-line expansion across recent fiscal periods [24, 27].

web_blocks.takeaway: Revenue compounded steadily from $5.14B to $8.75B, but FCF averaged ~$170M/year across FY2021–FY2025 as higher CapEx ($79.3M in FY25 vs. $34.3M in FY21) and working capital absorbed cash [24, 27, 40].

web_blocks.html: Balance Sheet, Goodwill & Debt Forensics: As of October 31, 2025, ABM carried $2,591.1 million in goodwill [17]. Stockholders' equity stood at $1,785.6 million, leaving goodwill at 145% of book equity [17]. Total balance-sheet debt stood at $1,566.5 million [17]. This total comprised $1,537.1 million in long-term debt and $29.4 million in current maturities [17]. The credit-facility leverage ratio ended FY2025 at 2.7x [28]. Leverage climbed to ~2.9x in FY2026 after funding the $275 million all-cash WGNSTAR acquisition [12, 36]. FY2025 net interest expense totaled $96.4 million against $325.2 million in GAAP operating profit [1, 37]. Interest coverage measures ~3.4x [1, 37]. While manageable, this coverage limits large debt-funded acquisitions until leverage declines toward 2.5x [37].

ROIC vs. Capital Allocation: ABM paid significant cash premiums above tangible net book value across multiple transactions [3]. Key acquisitions included GCA, Able, RavenVolt, Quality Uptime, and WGNSTAR [3, 11, 12]. Consequently, invested capital expanded faster than underlying operating profits [3]. This dynamic keeps trailing ROIC at ~4.62% alongside an ROE of 9.19% [3]. This return trails a typical 7.5%–8.5% industrial cost of capital [3]. Recent acquisitions functioned as strategic repositioning rather than high-return economic compounding [3]. Positively, ABM avoided shareholder dilution [3, 38]. Diluted share count declined from 68.0 million in FY2021 to 62.7 million in FY2025 [3, 38]. Basic shares totaled ~58.6 million in 2026 following steady repurchases [3, 38]. The company also extended its annual dividend streak to 58 consecutive years [38, 39].

web_blocks.title: FORENSIC WATCHPOINTS: GOODWILL, EARN-OUTS & CAPEX CREEP
paragraphs: 1. Goodwill Overhang: $2.59B in goodwill equals 145% of equity [17]. Commercial office distress could trigger balance-sheet impairments, mirroring the FY2020 write-down [17].
2. CapEx Step-Up: Property additions expanded from $34.3M in FY2021 to $79.3M in FY2025 [24, 27]. Technology outlays for the ELEVATE rollout drove this step-up [24, 27].
3. M&A Integration Discipline: ABM deployed $275M on WGNSTAR in February 2026 [12]. Management must generate organic cash flow without repeating earlier ERP or earn-out delays [12].

book_paragraphs: Put ten years of ABM Industries' audited financial statements side by side, and the entire story snaps into sharp focus. Back in fiscal 2016, ABM was a $5.14 billion building maintenance company generating $57 million in net income and roughly $116 million in operating cash flow. Ten years later, in fiscal 2025, revenue had climbed 70% to $8.75 billion, and net income reached $162.4 million. On the surface, that looks like steady, dependable industrial growth.

Look closer at the cash flow column, however, and you will spot the hidden cost of ABM's transformation. Over the past five years (FY2021 through FY2025), operating cash flow bounced wildly—from $314 million in FY2021 down to $20 million in FY2022, then stabilizing in a narrow band between $227 million and $243 million from FY2023 to FY2025. Meanwhile, capital expenditures more than doubled from $34.3 million in FY2021 to $79.3 million in FY2025 to fund the ELEVATE software overhaul. The result? Free cash flow averaged roughly $155 million to $190 million over the last three years—modest for a company doing nearly $9 billion in sales.

Now turn the page to the balance sheet, because that is where the roll-up bill comes due. Decades of acquisitions—GCA, Able, RavenVolt, Quality Uptime, and now WGNSTAR—left ABM with $2,591.1 million of goodwill on its October 2025 balance sheet, compared to $1,785.6 million of stockholders' equity. Total debt stood at $1,566.5 million before the $275 million WGNSTAR outlay in February 2026. Servicing that debt cost $96.4 million in annual interest, eating nearly a third of GAAP operating profit.

This explains the single most important forensic metric in our entire audit: ABM's return on invested capital sits at just 4.62%. When a business earns less than 5% on its total invested capital—below its cost of capital—acquisitions are buying scale and strategic positioning, not high-return economic moats. To management's credit, ABM has not funded this growth by diluting shareholders: diluted share count fell from 68.0 million in FY2021 to 62.7 million in FY2025, and the company has raised its dividend for 58 consecutive years. Yet the forensic verdict is clear: ABM is a resilient, cash-generating cyclical-and-contract operator, not an asset-light compounder.

book_subsections.title: The Forensic Verdict on Business Quality
paragraphs: Across Chapters 1 through 6, we have deliberately ignored stock prices and valuation multiples to judge ABM purely as an operating business. What have we found? ABM is a durable, essential-services leader with genuine bright spots in Aviation, Manufacturing & Distribution, and Technical Solutions. Its 58-year dividend streak proves its survival across every recession since 1968.

At the same time, its 1.86% net margin, 4.62% ROIC, 145% goodwill-to-equity ratio, and commercial office exposure in B&I mean that business quality is conditional on execution, deleveraging, and mix shift—not an automatic compounder.

book_subsections.title: The Goodwill Anchor: Understanding Why 4.62% ROIC Matters
paragraphs: If there is one number in Chapter 6 that you should circle in red ink, it is $2.59 billion of goodwill against $1.79 billion of shareholders' equity. When a company grows through serial acquisitions—buying GCA Services in 2017, Able Services in 2021, RavenVolt in 2022, and WGNSTAR more recently—the accounting rules require the buyer to record the purchase price above tangible book value as goodwill on the balance sheet.

Goodwill doesn't depreciate every year on the income statement, which makes adjusted EPS look clean. But it sits permanently in the denominator of Return on Invested Capital. When ABM earns roughly $230 million to $250 million of net operating profit after tax on more than $5 billion of invested capital, the math spits out a 4.62% ROIC—well below an 8.5% cost of capital.

That single ratio explains the entire history of ABM's valuation. Businesses that earn 30% ROIC can reinvest every dollar of profit at high rates and compound for decades. Businesses that earn 4.6% ROIC cannot compound rapidly through M&A; they create value only when they stop buying goodwill, harvest free cash flow from their existing footprint, pay down debt, and return cash to shareholders via dividends and opportunistic buybacks.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Our price-blind forensic audit is complete. ABM Industries is neither a broken business nor an elite compounder—it is a resilient, leveraged, 1.9%-net-margin services giant executing a multi-year pivot toward technical power and cleanroom infrastructure. With this unvarnished operational baseline locked in, we are finally ready to lift the blindfold in Pass 2 and ask what price makes sense for this exact set of economics.
